consensus_summary: Consensus responses split without a settled primary: either the false prophet/lying teacher (explicitly Isa 9:15) or subordinate/inferior status opposite the head (Deut 28:13, 44), with common alternatives for satanic sweeping deception (Rev 12:4) and tormenting/destructive power (Rev 9 tails).
book_summary: Tail is the prophet that teacheth lies (Isaiah’s own decode), head and tail already defined by the covenant (obedience makes Israel head not tail; curse inverts); applied so the dragon’s tail is the misleading that destroys the led, the trumpet serpent-tails that “had heads” are the liar enthroned, and Moses seizes the serpent by the tail.
consensus_core_identification: false prophet/deception or inferior/subordinate status (two co-equal common strands)
boundary_disagreement: Book folds the Deuteronomy head/tail polarity and the Revelation tail images into extensions of the single Isaiah false-prophet identification; consensus frequently lists those as independent parallel meanings.
rationale: Minimum cores match the Isaiah 9:15 referent that every consensus response already lists as primary or common alternative; the book’s added linkages and applications refine precision and reclassify the extension of that same referent rather than replace it or introduce an uncovered identification.
strongest_objection: Responses that treat the Deuteronomy status idiom as the more widespread or primary meaning may view the book’s elevation of the Isaiah decode (and consequent re-reading of the other passages) as over-narrowing.
